prerequisites: Complete the source installation on the start page: Node.js 22+, npm, Git, then npm ci and npm run build.
Use Bash on macOS/Linux or WSL, at the cloned repository root. Keep every step in the same terminal.
Use a fresh tutorial project name. If init/create says the project already exists, choose a new slug and update INSTRILO_PROJECT; do not delete work you want to keep.

next.label: Inspect the tutorial fixtures and checks

title: Move a working tool agent to LangGraph
summary: Switch frameworks while retaining guidance, connections, tool contracts and observable behavior.
outcome: A native tool agent and a real LangGraph StateGraph produce the same tested order answer with framework-specific traces.

verification.scope: The commands first run the native TypeScript agent, then safely regenerate and install the actual @langchain/langgraph package, execute its StateGraph and verify its model/tool node trace. The checked-in verify.mjs helper only reads saved JSON and asserts the expected results.
limitations: The deterministic fixture checks integration behavior, not model intelligence or response quality.
No paid model account, real credentials or cloud resource is used. Package installation still needs registry access.
The model replies are deterministic; LangGraph itself is a real installed dependency and executes during verification.
The generated graph has no external durable checkpointer. It does not promise cross-process graph-state resume merely because it uses LangGraph.

steps.title: Create the project
steps.body: This starts from a known native configuration so you can observe the framework change clearly.
steps.code:
set -eu
INSTRILO_PROJECT=.studio/tutorials/langgraph-agent
node dist/cli.js init langgraph-agent --directory .studio/tutorials
test -f "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/agent-studio.yaml"
steps.expected: The project starts with framework: native.

steps.title: Start the named local demonstration service
steps.body: This checked-in helper runs on an available localhost port. It returns deterministic model replies and synthetic order data. It is a demonstration service, not a real LLM. The EXIT trap stops only its tracked process if a later command fails.
steps.code:
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs serve "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.log" 2>&1 &
INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID=$!
trap 'kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs wait "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs files "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections"
export INSTRILO_TUTORIAL_BEARER=tutorial-bearer
steps.expected: The helper prints “Local deterministic fixture is ready” and writes five JSON connection/tool documents containing its actual local port.

steps.title: Connect the model route and the lookup tool
steps.body: The HTTP endpoint contains one synthetic order. The tool is read-only, has no required scopes and needs no approval in this local example. Real private data needs endpoint authentication and authorization appropriate to its users.
steps.code:
node dist/cli.js connections add answering "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/tool-runtime.json"
node dist/cli.js connections use runtime answering "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js tools add "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/lookup-tool.json"
node dist/cli.js tools list "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js validate "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: lookup_order is configured as a GET tool with a strict orderId schema. Project validation reports valid: true.

steps.title: Run the native baseline
steps.body: Keep the baseline output so the framework change has an observable comparison.
steps.code:
node dist/cli.js build "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js prepare "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js run "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --input 'Where is order ORD-1042?' > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/native-run.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs native-baseline "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: The native result records model, tool, model and the expected shipping answer.

steps.title: Switch, review regeneration and install LangGraph
steps.body: Configuration changes make old builds stale. Regeneration previews the file changes; --overwrite applies safe regeneration and still refuses conflicting edits. Prepare installs the newly declared framework dependency.
steps.code:
node dist/cli.js config set framework langgraph "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js generation plan "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node dist/cli.js build "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --overwrite
node dist/cli.js prepare "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs graph-package "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: Regeneration succeeds and the generated package declares @langchain/langgraph. Preparation resolves its real dependency.

steps.title: Execute the graph and compare results
steps.body: The graph now runs model and tools nodes. It uses the same portable tool schema and gateway transport as the native runtime.
steps.code:
node dist/cli.js run "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --input 'Where is order ORD-1042?' > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/langgraph-run.json"
cat "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/langgraph-run.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs graph-run "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs stats "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture-stats.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs graph-requests "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: The graph returns the same answer, records langgraph.model, tool, langgraph.model, and the fixture has observed two lookups across both runs.

steps.title: Stop the fixture you started
steps.body: Keep the generated project and evidence. Stop only this tutorial process; no broad process matching or machine cleanup is needed.
steps.code:
kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID"
wait "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" || true
trap - EXIT
printf 'Tutorial fixture stopped. Project files are retained.
'
steps.expected: The fixture stops and project files remain in .studio/tutorials.

troubleshooting: If preparation cannot reach npm/PyPI, fix registry/proxy access and repeat prepare; it does not require model credentials.
If the project already exists, inspect or keep it and choose a new tutorial slug. Do not rerun init over an existing manifest.
A demo runtime cannot use LangGraph; configure a supported API/gateway runtime before switching, as this guide does.
If you edit generated source before switching, inspect generation plan conflicts rather than deleting your changes.
cleanup: The final step stops the fixture. Both native-run.json and langgraph-run.json remain available to compare.
